source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Match assignments to acuity, workload, and nurse competency; many critically ill clients require about one nurse for two patients.","B":"Use the same routine patient load as a general medical-surgical unit because ICU acuity does not change staffing needs.","C":"Assign every critically ill client permanently one-to-one regardless of condition, therapy, workload, or available support.","D":"Use a fixed ratio alone without considering patient acuity, workload, nurse competency, or changes in clinical condition."}}
source_row.rationale: AACN staffing standards emphasize matching nursing assignments to current patient needs, workload, and nurse competency; critically ill patients generally require approximately one nurse for every two patients, with some requiring more intensive staffing. Option A is correct. B underestimates acuity, while C and D incorrectly make staffing an inflexible rule.
source_row.source_detail: Critical-care staffing standards: critically ill/injured patients generally require about one nurse for every two patients; assignments must reflect patient needs/acuity, workload, and nurse competency, with additional support for nurses new to a unit. AACN staffing standards published 2024-04-23 and current; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN 2026 Management of Care assignment/competency check completed first. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
